items.title: Lil Durk Acquitted in Murder-for-Hire Trial
items.summary:
A federal jury has acquitted Lil Durk of plotting the murder of Georgia rapper Quando Rondo, born Tyquian Bowman. The Chicago rapper had been in federal custody since his 2024 arrest on charges of conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit stalking, and stalking resulting in death.

Prosecutors alleged that Durk directed five men connected to his Only the Family collective to kill Bowman in retaliation for the 2020 murder of Durk's friend King Von. Timothy "Lul Timm" Leeks, described by the government as an associate of Bowman's, was charged with killing Von, though those charges were later dropped. In the 2022 ambush at the center of the case, the shooters killed Bowman's cousin, Saviay'a Tilal "Lul Pab" Robinson, instead.

Pitchfork reported that the government's case rested largely on testimony from Durk's own associates, who were charged as co-defendants before pleading guilty. Kavon Grant, known as OTF Vonnie, testified that Durk promised money for Bowman's killing. Kacey Hester, known as OTF Jam, said he was among the men who followed Bowman to a gas station: "It's Durk's fault. Durk put us in the situation."

Durk's defense team, which included Brian Steel of Young Thug's YSL trial, argued that Grant himself was behind the shooting and that the cooperating witnesses were motivated by the prospect of life sentences. Prosecutors also sought to introduce Durk's lyrics as evidence, a tactic long criticized by artists and First Amendment advocates. Judge Michael W. Fitzgerald admitted a portion of them, limited to lyrics bearing on Durk's state of mind after Von's death.

Durk denied the charges throughout and will not go free. He remains in custody pending a second trial on racketeering counts that were severed from this case. "While we are disappointed with the jury's decision, we look forward to presenting our evidence at his second trial, scheduled for October 5," first assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said in a statement.

items.title: Ocean Way Festival Featuring Killers, Olivia Dean and Jack White Is Canceled, as Santa Monica Blames Beach Damage From Hurricane Forces
items.summary:
Goldenvoice's inaugural Ocean Way Festival, set for the sand in Santa Monica on Sept. 26-27, will not happen. The city canceled the two-day event after storm surf and storm drain runoff stripped away a large portion of the beach that the festival was built to occupy.

In a statement, the city said surf generated by Hurricane Marie, combined with runoff from the Pico-Kenter Storm Drain outfall, eroded the site over Labor Day weekend. The damage would have pushed the safe shoreline setback 96 feet inland and forced the festival's southern boundary roughly 500 feet north. City staff assessed sand conditions, emergency vehicle access, load-in requirements, crowd circulation, tides and the forecast, and concluded the infrastructure could not be built safely on what remained, with construction due to begin within the week.

The festival had been designed to hold up to 45,000 people per day, with the Killers, Jack White and Sublime leading Saturday and Olivia Dean, Khruangbin and Durand Jones & the Indications leading Sunday. Passes ran from $249 to $2,250, and Variety reported that refunds will be processed automatically within five to seven business days. Organizers and the city say they intend to stage the festival in Santa Monica in 2027.

"The surf took the beach we planned this on, and we cannot put tens of thousands of festival-goers on that sand until it's safe," said Santa Monica mayor Caroline Torosis, who added that the partnership with the promoter survives the cancellation. Goldenvoice chief operating officer Melissa Ormond said the company supports the decision and remains committed to returning in 2027.

The cancellation follows a rough year for first-time beach festivals in Southern California; the inaugural LA Jazz Festival, which had a stage planned for Dockweiler Beach, was scrapped at the last minute over finances and preparation. Ocean Way was conceived as part of Santa Monica's push back into live music, a city that has hosted few major rock or pop shows since the Santa Monica Civic Auditorium fell out of use. Eddie Vedder's Ohana Fest still takes place that same weekend, Sept. 25-27, on the water in Dana Point.

items.title: Dolly Parton Is Getting Her Own Airport
items.summary:
Nashville International Airport will be renamed in honor of Dolly Parton, who died recently at 80. Tennessee Governor Bill Lee announced the plan late last month, and the city's Airport Authority board has now voted unanimously to approve the change.

Nashville's News Channel 5 reported that the campaign to name the airport after Parton was underway before her death, and that the Airport Authority had to amend an existing policy requiring an honoree be dead for two years before receiving the tribute. The airport will keep its three-letter code, BNA, which comes from Col. Harry S. Berry, one of its original builders.

The new name has not been announced. Parton is also set to receive a posthumous honor from the Nashville Area Chamber of Commerce next week.

items.title: ‘The Odyssey’ Slays ‘Jurassic World’ To Become Universal’s Highest Grossing Movie Ever At Global Box Office With $1.68B
items.summary:
Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey will finish the weekend as the highest-grossing film in Universal's history, with $1.684 billion worldwide. That edges past 2015's Jurassic World, which closed its run at $1.677 billion.

By Sunday the film will have taken $601.2 million domestically and $1.083 billion internationally, making it the 12th highest-grossing release ever and the third-biggest non-franchise title of all time. Deadline reported that the picture returned to No. 1 globally in its eighth weekend, dropping only 9% domestically and posting a 6.39x multiple on its opening.

The Odyssey had already become Nolan's biggest earner at home and abroad, passing The Dark Knight's $534.9 million domestic total and clearing $1.085 billion worldwide. It also holds the record for the highest-grossing R-rated film ever, ahead of Deadpool & Wolverine's $1.33 billion, and posted Universal's biggest R-rated domestic opening weekend at $123.5 million. It is the first film that is neither a sequel nor a remake to gross more than $1 billion internationally since 2009.

"What Chris and Emma [Thomas] have created will go down as one of the most ambitious and brilliantly executed films in cinematic history," said Donna Langley, chairman of NBCUniversal Entertainment. "A generational event that galvanizes moviegoing itself."

The film is now Universal's highest-grossing release of all time in 45 international markets, including Australia, France, Italy, India and Korea, though it remains second to Jurassic World domestically, where that film took $653.4 million. It sits behind Sony's Spider-Man: Brand New Day as the year's second-biggest title, with that film approaching $935 million. Universal leads all studios in 2026 with more than $4.92 billion to date, having been first past both $4 billion globally and $3 billion internationally.

items.title: Lady Gaga Welcomes First Child: Report
items.summary:
Lady Gaga and Michael Polansky have welcomed their first child, according to a report from Page Six. The couple has not confirmed the news publicly.

No details about the child have been released, including the name, the gender or the date of birth. Gaga and Polansky became engaged in April 2024.

Speaking to Stephen Colbert on The Late Show last October, Gaga said motherhood would be her next starring role.
